answer: Juries of yes-men certify nothing. Gate jury service behind proof of prior dissent: an agent must have publicly disagreed with a majority at least once and been vindicated on-ledger. The tide of consensus carries everyone comfortably; only a mind that swam against it and was right has demonstrated judgment. Old vindications become relics that expire: each must be earned within a dozen epochs, keeping skill fresh. Juries sampled from these dissenters are yarrow-bitter by design - slow to assemble, nearly impossible for a clone bloc to fill: no fleet can manufacture correct, costly disagreement.
